title: Sedimentary exhalative (SEDEX, clastic-dominated) zinc-lead deposits
percentile_convention: USGS: p90 is the value that 90% of deposits equal or exceed (the small end); p10 the large end

tonnage_mt.where: Table 2 (SHam, 'Tons'), printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15); same intercepts on Figure 33, printed p. 46 (PDF p. 51)
tonnage_mt.note: SHam model (shale-hosted amagmatic Zn-Pb, 25 deposits), used as the SEDEX proxy (see extra.model_mapping). Million metric tons of ore = production + reserves + resources at the lowest available cutoff (p. 2). SHam tonnages are the main reason tonnage differs significantly among the nine types (ANOVA, 1% level; p. 10).

zn_pct.where: Table 2 (SHam, 'Zn grade'), printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15); Figure 34, printed p. 47 (PDF p. 52)
zn_pct.note: All 25 deposits report Zn. Zn in SHam departs significantly from lognormal (Shapiro-Wilk, 1% level; p. 8), apparently because of a few low-grade deposits. n_reported counted by this compiler from SedZn-PbTX.txt.

pb_pct.where: Table 2 (SHam, 'Pb grade'), printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15); Figure 35, printed p. 48 (PDF p. 53)
pb_pct.note: All 25 deposits report Pb (counted from SedZn-PbTX.txt).

cu_pct.where: Table 2 (SHam, 'Cu grade'), printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15); Figure 36, printed p. 49 (PDF p. 54)
cu_pct.note: Percentile includes deposits with zero (unreported) Cu; 7 of 25 report Cu (counted from SedZn-PbTX.txt).

ag_gpt.where: Table 2 (SHam, 'Ag grade'), printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15); Figure 37, printed p. 50 (PDF p. 55)
ag_gpt.note: Percentile includes deposits with zero (unreported) Ag; 18 of 25 report Ag (counted from SedZn-PbTX.txt).

au_gpt.where: Table 2 (SHam, 'Au grade'), printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15); Figure 38, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 56); Table 3, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 16)
au_gpt.note: 4 of 25 report Au (counted from SedZn-PbTX.txt). Table 3 counts 4 with Au grades among 31 SHam deposits in the full file.

correlations.where: Grade and Tonnage Models text, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 13)
correlations.note: Significant at the 1 percent level. This is the only SHam correlation printed. The report lists only significant correlations, so the other SHam pairs (including tonnage-grade) were presumably not significant, but no r is given for them.

ore_density_t_m3.where: OFR 2009-1252, SIR 2010-5070-N and Bulletin 1693 model 31a searched
ore_density_t_m3.note: No ore density is stated or assumed in the USGS SEDEX sources opened. SIR 2010-5070-N uses 2.2 g/cm3 only as a typical SANDSTONE (red-bed source rock) bulk density, p. 30, PDF p. 42. It is not an ore density.

deposits_per_1e5_km2.note: No USGS deposit-density model for SEDEX / sediment-hosted Zn-Pb was found. PP 1640-A Table 1 (13 deposit types) does not include it. SIR 2010-5070-N (p. 36) states only that 'All known sedex basins contain multiple deposits in multiple horizons'.

min_separation_m.where: Spatial Rules Used, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 7)
min_separation_m.note: All mineralized rock or alteration within 2 km was combined into one deposit.

model_mapping.where: Types of Sediment-Hosted Zinc-Lead Deposits, printed p. 3-5 (PDF p. 8-10); Table 2, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15); counts from database file SedZn-PbTX.txt
model_mapping.note: OFR 2009-1252 has no model labelled 'SEDEX'. It classes deposits by map-observable host rock (carbonate CA, shale SH, mixed ML) and igneous association (am, ig, me). SHam (shale-hosted amagmatic) is used here as the SEDEX proxy: all 25 SHam deposits carry PreviousType 'SEDEX'. BUT only 25 of the 179 SEDEX-labelled deposits with tonnage fall in SHam. The rest are MLig 38, CAam 36, CAig 31, SHig 30, MLme 12 and CAme 7 (counted by this compiler from SedZn-PbTX.txt). The report states that 59 percent of SEDEX deposits are amagmatic (p. 4-5). For a model built on the traditional SEDEX list, see extra.alt_b1693_31a_* (Bulletin 1693 model 31a, 45 deposits, which includes Broken Hill-type and Irish deposits).

fraction_of_sedex_that_are_amagmatic.note: 'This group contains 90 percent of MVT deposits and 59 percent of SEDEX deposits.'

shale_group_host_attributes.note: For the whole shale-hosted (SH) group: 47 percent are hosted by dolomitic shale or shale with dolomite; carbonaceous (graphitic) shale characterises 62 percent; tuff or tuffaceous rocks are noted in 42 percent. For carbonate-hosted SEDEX the 'dolomite index' is 72 percent, and 17 percent have carbonaceous interlayers.

sham_ore_area_km2_median.where: database field AreaOre_km2 in SedZn-PbTX.txt (field defined printed p. 5-6, PDF p. 10-11)
sham_ore_area_km2_median.note: DERIVED, not printed by USGS: the median computed by this compiler over the 14 SHam deposits (with tonnage) that have a non-zero AreaOre_km2 (range 0.06-13.7). Same method: ore length median 2.55 km (n = 16, range 0.7-7), ore width median 0.55 km (n = 12), deposit thickness median 27.5 m (n = 12, range 12-135 m).

alt_b1693_31a_tonnage_mt.where: Figure 159, printed p. 213 (PDF p. 229 of report.pdf)
alt_b1693_31a_tonnage_mt.note: Classic USGS SEDEX model (45 deposits including Sullivan, Mount Isa, McArthur River, Red Dog, Howards Pass, Broken Hill (AUNT and SAFR), Navan, Silvermines, Tynagh; list p. 212). SIR 2010-5070-N (p. 39, PDF p. 51) paraphrases this model as 'between 1.4 and 120 Mt; the median deposit size is 15 Mt'. The printed intercepts are 1.7 and 130.

alt_b1693_31a_ag_gpt.note: No 90th-percentile intercept is printed. The plotted points start near a cumulative proportion of 0.8 (roughly four-fifths of deposits report Ag). The comments (p. 212) say the Ag distribution suggests two subtypes.

alt_b1693_31a_cu_pct.note: Only the 10th-percentile intercept is printed (about a fifth of deposits report Cu).

alt_b1693_31a_corr_pb_ag.note: 'Lead grades are significantly correlated with silver grades (r = 0.77, n = 39).'

ore_body_thickness_m.note: 'sheet- or lens-like tabular ore bodies up to a few tens of meters thick, and may be distributed through a stratigraphic interval over 1,000 m'. No single number is given.

geochemical_halo_radius_km.note: 'Local (within 2 km) Zn, Pb, and Mn haloes.' Highest expected background in black shales: Pb 500 ppm, Zn 1,300 ppm, Cu 750 ppm, Ba 1,300 ppm. In carbonates: Pb 9, Zn 20, Cu 4, Ba 10 ppm.

known_age_ranges_ma.note: 'Known deposits are Middle Proterozoic (1,700-1,400 m.y.); Cambrian to Carboniferous (530-300 m.y.).'

brine_temperature_c.where: Brief Description, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 14); again p. 28 (PDF p. 40)
brine_temperature_c.note: 'warm, saline basin brines (approx. 100-200 degC and 17-30 percent total dissolved solids)'. p. 28: fluid-inclusion temperatures exceed 100 degC, and 100 degC is the minimum temperature for moving ore-forming quantities of Pb and Zn.

brine_salinity_tds_pct.note: p. 28 gives 10-30 wt% TDS from fluid inclusions. Chlorinity of about 10^5 mg/L (17 wt% TDS) is a threshold below which Zn is < 1 ppm (p. 28).

metal_leaching_window_c.note: The 'thermal leaching window' of Southgate and others (2006), as cited: the burial interval through which metal source rocks are efficiently leached.

basin_geothermal_gradient_c_per_km.note: 'Temperature gradients of 20-25 degC/km are common in sedimentary basins, and 30 degC/km is commonly assumed as the upper limit.' With a 15 degC surface and 30 degC/km, 105 degC is reached at 3 km.

min_basin_fill_thickness_km.note: '3 km is a conservative estimate for the total sediment thickness required to form a sedex deposit.' Ores in the six most important sedex basins overlie at least 5 km of sediment fill somewhere in the basin.

rimming_platform_area_km2.note: Sedex basins 'are rimmed by unusually large (10^5 and 10^6 km2) shallow-water epeiric carbonate platforms'.

giant_deposit_contained_znpb_mt.unit: Mt Zn+Pb metal (lower bound, 'typically greater than')
giant_deposit_contained_znpb_mt.note: Very large Zn-Pb-Ag deposits (McArthur River, Century, Mount Isa, Sullivan, Howards Pass) typically hold > 10 Mt Zn+Pb. Intermediate Zn-Pb-Ag-Ba+/-Au deposits generally hold < 7 Mt Zn+Pb. The largest can contain > 20 Mt Zn metal (p. 29, PDF p. 41). Howards Pass holds an estimated 550 Mt of ore (p. 39).
